shill: udev: remove device "reloader" This was implemented with the expectation that we'd add custom uevents into the kernel (e.g., CL:187492). But those were never merged [1]. In the meantime, mwifiex has picked up automatic reset support entirely within the kernel (it already had it for SDIO [2]; it has now been implemented for PCIe via Function Level Reset [3]). (These scripts were seemingly added only for mwifiex + PCIe, but incidentally, I believe all other Wifi drivers have similar automatic reset mechanisms that don't require the help of user-space like this.) Drop these scripts. [1] See for example, the TEST= line for CL:187474, which implies that the test required local driver hacks. Grepping src/third_party/kernel/v* yields no instance of the "device_hang" event. [2] Upstream Linux commit, in kernel v3.8: d31ab3577eca mwifiex: add support for SDIO card reset [3] CL:475016 CQ-DEPEND=CL:493794 BUG=none TEST=Wifi (including 'reset' functionality) on Kevin; e.g., force a command timeout like the following, and see mwifiex recover: `iw mlan0 scan > /dev/null & cat /sys/kernel/debug/mwifiex/mlan0/device_dump` TEST=`echo 1 > /sys/bus/pci/devices/0000\:01\:00.0/reset` Change-Id: I88b603d2afdb61f59f9dde71ae1f543748c04660 Signed-off-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/493888 Reviewed-by: Paul Stewart <pstew@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Ben Chan <benchan@chromium.org>

run_oci: remove signature checking We always use the unsigned option because signature checking is done when imageloader mounts the squashfs image rather than at run_oci time. For VMs, this checking happens outside of the VM so we've already done it by the time run_oci is called in that case as well. This also removes the need to have libcrypto in the deps. FROMGIT: kbuild: clang: add -no-integrated-as to KBUILD_[AC]FLAGS The Linux Kernel relies on GCC's acceptance of inline assembly as an opaque object which will not have any validation performed on the content. The current behaviour in LLVM is to perform validation of the contents by means of parsing the input if the MC layer can handle it. Disable clangs integrated assembler and use the GNU assembler instead. eclass: Change CROS_FIRMWARE_SCRIPT default to updater4.sh. Most Chromebooks are using updater4.sh today and we've already deprecated updater1 and updater2. ChromeOS firmware architecture is more stable now so we can expect the need of having another "updater version" may be not necessary in future that it may be possible to merge all versions back into single implementation. As the first step, we should let CROS_FIRMWARE_SCRIPT default to the "common implementation", i.e., updater4, and then remove the CROS_FIRMWARE_SCRIPT for ebuild files using updater4 in overlay. FROMLIST: fix minor error in YUV2RGB matrix used in shader The matrix used for YCbCr to RGB is listed in Wiki https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YCbCr; There is minor error in the matrix constant: 0.0625=16/256 should be 16.0/255, and 0.5=128.0/256 should be 128.0/255. Note that conversion from a 0-255 byte number to 0-1.0 float is to divide by 255 instead of 256. That's we get 255=1.0f. By the constant change we can see the CSC result is bit aligned with Wiki conversion result and FFMPeg result. Otherwise in some situation, there will be one bit difference Bugzilla: https://bugs.freedesktop.org/show_bug.cgi?id=100854 Signed-off-by: Kristian H. shill: make ShillDaemon use DaemonTask instead of inheriting from it Most of the daemon logic is implemented in DaemonTask. ShillDaemon simply calls DaemonTask::Init() and DaemonTask::Quit(). As the public interface of DaemonTask doesn't need to be exposed through ShillDaemon, ShillDaemon doesn't really need to inherit from DaemonTask. This CL changes ShillDaemon to own a private instance of DaemonTask instead, which also eliminates the multiple inheritance in ShillDaemon. This CL adds DISALLOW_COPY_AND_ASSIGN to ShillDaemon and DaemonTask. BUG=None TEST=Run unit tests and manually test starting/stopping shill on device. CHROMIUM: PM / OPP: Fix lockdep warning logic Each build spits out the following warning several times. drivers/base/power/opp/core.c: In function '_find_device_opp': drivers/base/power/opp/core.c:36:41: warning: suggest parentheses around '&&' within '||' [-Wparentheses] RCU_LOCKDEP_WARN(!rcu_read_lock_held() && \ ^ include/linux/rcupdate.h:550:52: note: in definition of macro 'RCU_LOCKDEP_WARN' if (debug_lockdep_rcu_enabled() && !__warned && (c)) { \ ^ drivers/base/power/opp/core.c:95:2: note: in expansion of macro 'opp_rcu_lockdep_assert' opp_rcu_lockdep_assert(NULL); ^ Looking closer at the code, the current logic doesn't really make much sense. It warns if !rcu_read_lock_held() _and_ (s && srcu_read_lock_held(s)), but also if !lockdep_is_held(&dev_opp_list_lock) even if rcu_read_lock_held() is true. That is a deviation from both the upstream code and the most recent version of the patch in patchwork. Replace the logic with https://patchwork.kernel.org/patch/7221501/. Note: Commit 03eb5b44e56f, which introduced this code, references this patch in patchwork but does not explain the change in logic. BUG=chrome-os-partner:50411 TEST=Build any target and observe lack of warning Rebase/upstream note: Does not apply to v4.11 or later kernels since the code has been reorganized. See upstream commit 052c6f19141d for details. Change-Id: I1976b59e3c7d666c6f73ca913cb0ed2670328aa2 Signed-off-by: Guenter Roeck <groeck@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/495375 Reviewed-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org>
